newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Aramco set to add new LPG term buyers - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Aramco set to add new LPG term buyers - MEES.

text.p: Saudi Aramco is set to add a number of new LPG contract buyers by next month, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.
"When the new year begins next month, chances are that Saudi Aramco will have added a dozen or so new companies to its already long list of LPG contract buyers," MEES said.
It said in recent months Aramco had made "substantial headway" in finding replacement buyers for over one million tonnes of product freed up by some cancellations earlier this year.

"It appears that four new contract customers have signed on to lift over 600,000 tonnes of LPG in 1997. In addition, advance discussions covering a further 400,000 tonnes of product are understood to be underway with three other firms."

Committed customers were Ferrell, for some 120,000 tonnes; Natural Gas Clearinghouse, with 180,000 tonnes; Indian Oil Corp with 100,000-150,000 tonnes a year of butane; and Glencore, with some 180,000 tonnes a year of propane starting in January.
MEES said other interested companies included France's Total, which is interested in up to 150,000 tonnes a year of LPG, and Trammo and Naftomar.

It said Aramco has been selling up to 200,000 tonnes a month of LPG on a spot basis since June this year when three of its major oil firm customers cancelled supply contracts totalling some 1.55 million tonnes annually.
